To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high-resolution SNP haplotype map was constructed for casein genes in the Norwegian Red population.
the CSN2-67 C allele is associated with increased milk and protein yields and that it should be increased in the Norwegian Red population.

we identified two distinct haplotype blocks in the bovine caseins region and that we identified a highly significant association between the CSN2 and milk production traits in the Norwegian Red breed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of haplotype structures in the bovine caseins and their associations with production traits.
the identification and characterization of genetic variation in the casein gene cluster in the bovine genome.
the genetic improvement of milk production traits and with the potential health effects of milk proteins on humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most significant association with milk production was found for the SNP in CSN2_66 with the A allele associated with both protein and total milk yield.

CSN2_66 and CSN2_68 (or haplotype blocks containing these SNPs) are associated with milk protein content and CSN2-66, CSN2_69 and CSN2 67 (or haplotypes containing these SNPs or haplotype blocks) are associated with both milk and protein yields.
the CSN2 gene, in particular the CSN2 67th amino acid, seems to be a good candidate for selective breeding to improve milk protein yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a SNP within the CSN2 gene that is significantly associated with both milk and protein yields and that is likely to be a causative mutation.

CSN2 and/or CSN1S 2 are likely the genes underlying the association with milk protein and milk production traits in our study population and that CSN2_ 67 is the SNP most strongly associated with these traits.
we have shown that the casein haplotype block CSN2-CSN3 is associated with milk production traits and that the SNP CSN1_67 (rs109) is the most likely candidate for the causative DNA variant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the haplotype block approach is an effective tool to identify regions of the genome associated with complex traits and to identify the causative DNA variation underlying these associations.

a high-resolution SNP map of the casein region is a valuable tool for studying haplotype structures, identifying haplotypes of interest and for the design of marker-assisted selection strategies for the improvement of milk protein and production in dairy cattle.
the haplotype structure within the casein cluster can be used for the detection of QTLs for milk production traits in cattle.
